title: EFTPOS Terminal Card-Read & Connectivity Fault — Store Triage SOP

source_document.ingestion_pipeline: AI Search hybrid ingestion (chunked, embedded, indexed)

summary: Structured triage and remediation steps for EFTPOS terminal hardware faults presenting as intermittent card-read failure, unresponsive display, or connectivity drop. Derived from recurring incident resolution patterns (e.g. INC-2026-08850) and validated across multiple store sites.

sections.heading: Symptom Triage
sections.content: Confirm the specific failure mode with the reporting team member: (a) terminal completely unresponsive / blank screen, (b) terminal powered on but intermittently fails to read chip or tap transactions, (c) terminal displays a persistent connectivity/offline error. Capture affected checkout/terminal ID and store ID before proceeding.

sections.heading: Step 1 — Power Cycle
sections.content: Instruct on-site staff to hold the power button for 10 seconds to force shutdown, wait 15 seconds, then power on. Allow up to 2 minutes for the terminal to reconnect to the store payment gateway. If this resolves the fault, monitor for recurrence over the next 48 hours before closing.

sections.heading: Step 2 — Cable and PIN Pad Connection Check
sections.content: If power cycling does not resolve an intermittent card-read failure, the most common root cause is a loose or partially seated PIN pad cable connection at the terminal base. Instruct staff (or dispatch a technician) to firmly reseat the cable connector, ensuring an audible click, then repeat Step 1 (power cycle). This step alone has resolved the majority of intermittent card-read incidents historically (see resolution pattern from INC-2026-08850).

sections.heading: Step 3 — Firmware and Network Check
sections.content: If the fault persists after Steps 1–2, check the terminal's firmware version against the current approved baseline via the Store Payments Platform device management console. Confirm the terminal has network connectivity to the payment gateway (ping/heartbeat check). Apply pending firmware updates if the terminal is out of date.

sections.heading: Step 4 — Hardware Swap Escalation
sections.content: If the fault recurs within 48 hours of a successful Step 1/2 fix, or if Steps 1–3 do not resolve the issue, escalate for a hardware swap. Log a request with the Store Technology Support hardware pool referencing this SOP ID and the original incident number. Do not leave a faulty terminal in active use — direct staff to route customers to an alternate checkout.

sections.heading: Customer Impact Handling
sections.content: While the terminal is faulted, advise staff to redirect customers to the nearest working checkout. If store-wide EFTPOS impact is suspected (multiple terminals affected simultaneously), escalate immediately as a potential P1 and notify the Store Operations Duty Manager — this may indicate a payment gateway or network-level fault rather than a single terminal hardware issue.
